ADR01
One encounter workspace
Use a task-centred mobile flow with person and encounter context fixed
Workers reuse facts across programmes; distinct patient records remain isolated
UI widgets and question packs require usability validation
ADR02
Modular server and durable workers
Start with a modular service and database-backed outbox workers
Reduces cross-service failure modes while preserving clear component contracts
Split components only when measured scale or custody requires it
ADR03
Canonical operational model
Persist typed operational entities and transform at adapter boundaries
Shared facts retain provenance while destinations keep independent schemas
Canonical shape is not itself an ABDM clinical document
ADR04
Native field client
Use an Android reference client with encrypted local storage and keystore wrapping
Offline lease and media recovery require controlled device behaviour
Web admin supports online work; browser storage is not the default clinical offline store
ADR05
Bounded planner
Separate model planning from deterministic execution and policy
Tool outputs and retrieved records cannot grant authority
Model vendor selected through performance privacy and cost review
ADR06
Independent destination actions
Use saga-style recovery and evidence-based reconciliation
No global atomic commit exists across unrelated programme systems
Uncertain results need lookup or manual resolution before retry
ADR07
Immutable confirmed revisions
Use append-only clinical fact revisions and approval hashes
Corrections remain attributable and invalidate affected work
Storage and retention policy must cover original and corrected versions
ADR08
Versioned capability activation
Activate provider and model version per deployment and scope
Evidence and local permission differ from a successful API test
Substitution requires equivalent approved intended use
ADR09
Explicit exchange scope
Implement ABDM and direct EHR as separate connector types
Consent or API availability does not grant universal records access
Exact external contracts stay blocked until owner verification
ADR10
Defence in depth authorisation
Use service policy and tenant RLS with separate runtime roles
Prevents client scope selection and catches tenant query errors
Tenant RLS does not replace patient relationship and purpose checks
ADR11
Operational metrics projection
Build controlled report projections from versioned domain events
Queries can disclose source completeness and avoid double counting
Late records require reproducible metric revision
ADR12
Explicit synthetic environment
Simulators emit mode and source markers and use isolated fixtures
Development can exercise failures before partner credentials exist
Simulation evidence cannot pass live connector or clinical validation gates
